body: Mainland China’s official coverage is shot with a tripod, resulting in motion blur and saturated colors. Coverage in Hong Kong and Macau uses Google Cars instead.
Chinese script uses complex symbols. Mainland China typically uses simplified Chinese characters, which have fewer strokes than traditional forms used in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and Macau.
Chinese licence plates are blue with white text.
Coverage in mainland China is limited, mostly around major eastern cities. Some areas are hidden on Google Maps but accessible via other mapping apps.
Much of the coverage is inside museums, mainly in Beijing and Shanghai but also in many other cities.
Historic ancient towns with coverage include Zhoucun, areas near Xuzhou, Yangzhou, west of Jiaxing, and west of Zhangzhou.
Modern urban area coverage is found in Beijing, Yangzhou, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Chengdu.
The Forbidden City (Palace Museum) is a prominent palace complex located in central Beijing.
Near Beijing’s Today Art Museum is a modern street lined with cafes, bars, and an uncanny statue out front.
The Sichuan Museum in Chengdu features a parking area with abundant greenery.
The Hubei Museum in Wuhan stands out due to its palace-style architecture and grey roofs.
The Museum of Silk in Hangzhou is known for its rounded glass facade and distinctive front fountain.
The Long Museum in Shanghai features a boxy concrete building design.
Suzhou Museum is recognized by its white and grey symmetrical angular design.
The Yangzhou Museum is distinguished by its beige, rounded stone exterior.
Zhoucun is the only pinpointable ancient city in China, recognized by its straight north-south street.
